items.pregunta: Is the size of the accepted upload, body or file limited before it is buffered, parsed or decompressed, and limited again after decompression?
items.evidencia: The size limit option or check and where it runs relative to the read

items.pregunta: Is the number of rows, items or pages one request or job processes bounded, so a single bulk or import request cannot run unbounded queries or downstream calls?
items.evidencia: The limit, page size or chunking applied to the loop or query

items.pregunta: Are the regular expressions and recursive parsers applied to user input free of nested quantifiers and unbounded depth, so one crafted value cannot hold the process?
items.evidencia: The regular expression or the depth limit of the parser

items.pregunta: Is expensive work (parsing large input, hashing, paid external calls) done only after authentication and the size or rate check?
items.evidencia: The order of the authentication and limit middlewares relative to the expensive call

items.pregunta: Are retries of failing jobs and downstream calls capped with backoff, and is a record that keeps failing set aside instead of blocking the queue or the job?
items.evidencia: The retry limit and backoff, and the dead-letter or skip branch

items.pregunta: Does a scheduled job avoid starting a new run while the previous one is still running, and stop when its time limit passes?
items.evidencia: The lock, overlap guard or timeout of the job
